blocking.section: Decision drivers (Budget safety); Decision outcome table (Token Budget row); Pros and cons (Post-response charging)
blocking.issue: The ADR treats the pack 8.9 overshoot bound and the owning document's bound as one bound, but they differ. The owning document adds (attempts - 1) x R per concurrent request for Provider Fallback, plus hidden reasoning on gemini and ollama. That term stays finite only because budgeted Routes allow at most 2 attempts and stop fallback with RZ-AI-005 once the attempts' usage reaches R. The ADR leaves out this attempt cap. Its Token Budget row keeps the single-attempt wording 'charges usage and releases the rest', which cannot hold when usage summed over two attempts exceeds R. Its rejection of option 5 also claims that R bounds per-request overshoot, which is false with Provider Fallback. As written, an implementer following the ADR alone can build unbounded per-request spend through retries times candidates.
blocking.evidence: ADR: "with overshoot bounded as pack 8.9 and the owning document's [Settlement](...) state (hypothesis; SM-10)"; Token Budget row: "`onLog` charges usage and releases the rest, or charges all of R and emits a degraded-state metric when usage is missing"; option 5: "which the reservation of R bounds under pack 8.9." Owning doc, Model routing: "a request makes at most (`retries.attempts` + 1) x candidates attempts. Until OQ-ai-llm-gateway-16 registers a cap, Routes with `ai.token-budget` allow 2 attempts (target) and stop Provider Fallback with `RZ-AI-005` once the attempts' usage, counting R for an attempt without usage, reaches R." Settlement: "plus (attempts - 1) x R per concurrent request ([Model routing](#model-routing); hypothesis)"; row 2: "All of R once per request, plus usage other attempts reported".
blocking.fix: In the Token Budget row, replace the onLog clause with: "`onLog` charges usage summed over attempts, plus all of R once if any attempt lacked usage (with the degraded-state metric), and releases the rest; budgeted Routes allow 2 attempts (target) and stop Provider Fallback with `RZ-AI-005` once that charge reaches R". In Budget safety, state the bound explicitly: "overshoot at most the sum of concurrent input-estimate errors plus (attempts - 1) x R per concurrent request (hypothesis; SM-10), as [Settlement](...) states; pack 8.9 omits the fallback term (OQ-ai-llm-gateway-15)". In option 5, write "which the reservation of R bounds per attempt".

blocking.issue: The decoder that resolves `model` against one Upstream's `ai.models` and `ai.surface` runs at the start of onRequestBody. That is before onRoute, where pack section 4 and the System overview select among a Route's Upstream legs. A Route may have more than one Upstream (weighted legs) or composition steps (pack section 3), and no document limits a Route with a `protocol: ai` Upstream to one leg. When two legs are `ai` Upstreams with different `surface` or `models`, the ADR does not say which decoder runs, which AIModel supplies C and E, or what R reserves. The decision table therefore cannot be implemented unambiguously.
blocking.evidence: ADR: "| Surface decoder | At the start of `onRequestBody`, before any Policy: strict JSON ..., `model` resolved in `ai.models` (`RZ-AI-001`), C computed, E only when a reader needs it |". Pack section 4: "body-dependent criteria choose only among its Upstream legs or `AIModel` candidates in `onRoute`." Pack section 3 Route: "one or more Upstreams, directly or through `composition`". System overview Phase table: "| `onRoute` | Once | Upstream leg or `AIModel` candidate selection |".
blocking.fix: Add one clause to the Surface decoder row, or to More information: "assumes a Route with a `protocol: ai` Upstream has exactly one upstream leg and no `composition`; the validation code is a proposed registration under OQ-ai-llm-gateway-16". This makes the decoder's Upstream unique before onRoute without inventing a field.
